and the moon, which imitates in a certain way the meeting of the sun and moon, and represents it in color. Thus all things are full of divine things: earthly things are indeed full of celestial things, and celestial things are full of super-celestial things, and every order of things proceeds even to the last. For those things which are gathered into one above the order of things, these are subsequently dilated in their descent, where other souls are ordered under other deities. Furthermore, there are many **solar animals**, such as **lions** and **roosters**, which participate in a certain solar deity according to their nature. Whence it is a wonder how much the lower things in the same order yield to the higher, even if they do not yield in size or power. From this, they say that the **rooster** is greatly feared by the **lion**, and almost worshipped; the cause of which thing we cannot assign to matter or sense, but only to the contemplation of the higher order: namely, because the presence of the solar power is more suited to the rooster than to the lion. This is also apparent because the rooster applauds the rising sun with certain hymns, as it were, and calls out, as it were, when the sun is turned toward us from the mid-heaven of the <term>antipodes</term> <note>the people or places on the opposite side of the earth.</note>. And sometimes certain solar angels have appeared, endowed with such forms; and though they themselves were without form within themselves, yet to us

# PROCLUS ON
<page-num>478</page-num>
<header>PROCLUS ON</header>

...we who are formed encounter those who are formed. Sometimes even solar demons have been seen with the face of a lion; yet when a **rooster** <note>In ancient "sympathetic" magic, the rooster was considered a solar animal because it heralds the sunrise, and thus it held power over lower solar spirits like these demons.</note> was set against them, they suddenly vanished. This happens because things that are lower in the same cosmic order always revere those that are higher—just as many people, when looking upon the images of divine men, are moved by that very sight to fear committing any shameful act.

To speak briefly, some things revolve along with the movements of the Sun, such as the plants we mentioned; others imitate the shape of solar rays in some way, like the **palm** and the **date**; others reflect the fiery nature of the Sun, like the **laurel**; and others reflect some other quality. One may clearly see that the properties gathered in the Sun are distributed far and wide among those following in the solar order: namely, among angels, demons, souls, animals, plants, and stones. 

For this reason, the authors of the ancient priesthood <note>Proclus refers here to the "Theurgists," practitioners of a type of Neoplatonic ritual magic intended to unite the soul with the divine.</note> discovered the worship of higher powers from these visible things, sometimes mixing them and other times using them for purification. They mixed many things together because they saw that simple, single objects possessed some property of a deity, yet were not sufficient on their own to summon that divinity.

---

<page-num>479</page-num>
<header>SACRIFICE AND MAGIC.</header>

Therefore, by this very mixture of many elements, they attracted heavenly influences. By composing one thing out of many, they made it similar to that "One" which sits above the many; they even constructed statues out of many blended materials. By skillfully gathering composite scents into a single divine symbol, they produced a result that reflects the divine essence—encompassing, as it does, many different powers. While the division of these elements weakens each one, their mixture restores them to the likeness of their original archetype.

Sometimes, however, a single herb or a single stone is enough for a divine work. For instance, the **thistle** <note>original: *Cnebifon*; likely a Latinized version of a Greek name for a specific ritual plant.</note> is sufficient for the sudden appearance of a deity. For protection, however, one uses the **laurel**, the **thorny shrub** <note>original: *Raccinum*</note>, the onion, the sea-squill, coral, diamond, and jasper. But for prophecy, the heart of a mole is used. For purification, sulphur and seawater are employed. 

Thus, the priests brought things together through their mutual kinship and "sympathy," <note>The concept that all things in the universe are interconnected by hidden "strings" or resonances.</note> while they expelled unwanted influences through "antipathy" or repugnance—purifying when necessary with sulphur and asphalt (that is, bitumen) and sprinkling with seawater. Indeed, sulphur purifies because of its sharp odor, while seawater purifies because of its fiery portion. And animals dedicated to the gods...

<summary>Proclus explains the "solar chain" of animals, plants, and minerals, and describes how ancient priests (theurgists) used the principle of "sympathy" to attract divine presence or purify spaces using specific natural materials like laurel, sulphur, and seawater.</summary>

# PROCLUS ON SACRIFICE
<page-num>480</page-num>
<header>PROCLUS ON SACRIFICE</header>
<header>FROM PORPHYRY, ON THE DESCENT AND ASCENT OF THE soul.</header>

...they applied things suitable for worship, and other such matters in a similar fashion. For this reason, receiving knowledge from these and similar things, they first recognized the powers of **daemons** <note>In the Neoplatonic tradition of Proclus, "daemons" are not evil spirits but intermediate beings that bridge the gap between the divine gods and the physical world.</note>, namely that these powers are closest to natural things and actions; and through these natural things, to which they are near, they summoned them into their presence. Then, from the daemons, they proceeded to the very powers and actions of the gods—partly learning by the instruction of the daemons, and partly through their own diligence, interpreting the appropriate **symbols** <note>original: "symbola." In this context, symbols are physical "tokens" or "signatures" placed in nature by the divine, which a practitioner can use to "tune" themselves to a specific god.</note>, ascending into a proper understanding of the gods. Finally, having left behind natural things and actions, and for the most part even the daemons, they were received into the company of the gods.

->AND MAGIC.<-

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut drop cap 'O' depicting a seated figure in a classical robe within a landscape of trees and hills.</image-desc>We ought (if indeed we are to return to those things which are truly our own) to entirely cast off these things which we have taken upon ourselves from our mortal nature, along with the inclination toward them through which our descent happened. Furthermore, we must remember our blessed and eternal substance. While we strive to ascend toward the incorporeal, we must meditate on two things in particular: first, by what method we may set aside that which is material and fleeting; and second, by what path we may especially return—namely, returning by a path contrary to the one by which we descended to these present things. For we were, and still are, pure intellectual essences, living far from all sense-perception and irrational nature. But we have been joined to a sensible <note>Meaning "perceived by the senses."</note> nature, partly through the weakness of our eternal connection to our own "intelligible" or divine part, and partly through a power that leans toward lower things. For all powers that act through the senses and the body only then begin to sprout into effect when the soul fails to persevere in the purely intellectual realm—much like a corrupted earth which, though it has often received wheat, finally yields only **weeds** <note>original: "lolium," referring to darnel or tares; a metaphor for the soul producing lower, "choking" impulses instead of divine thoughts.</note>.

<meta>This page continues the excerpt from Porphyry (a 3rd-century Neoplatonist philosopher and student of Plotinus) regarding the soul's ascent. ### FROM PORPHYRY.

This happens through a certain depravity of the soul, which indeed does not lose its own essence while an irrational sprout buds forth, but through this very thing the soul is joined with mortality, being drawn from its own nature toward that which is foreign. Therefore, if we ever strive with all our strength to return to our original state, it is necessary to entirely separate the mind from sense, imagination, and every irrational condition that follows from them, as well as from passions of that kind, as far as the necessity of nature permits. We must rightly arrange and articulately compose those things which pertain to the mind, establishing through this a beautiful tranquility and peace regarding the irrational part. The goal is that we might not only hear about the **intelligible things** <note>original: "intelligibilibus." In Neoplatonism, "intelligible things" are the ultimate realities—the Forms or Ideas—that can only be perceived by the intellect, not the physical senses.</note> of the intellect, but also realize how great a power we are. By enjoying the contemplation of the mind and being restored to an incorporeal nature, we may now truly live through the intellect, no longer living falsely alongside perishable and related natures. We must, therefore, loosen many garments <note>Porphyry uses the metaphor of "garments" or "robes" (indumenta) to describe the layers of ego, physical sensation, and emotion that the soul "puts on" as it descends into the material world.</note> from ourselves: both this visible garment of the body and the interior robes we still wear. For we must not only avoid the effects of vices, but we must even root out the effects themselves. The departure from the body can indeed happen with 
<meta>catchword: violence</meta>

violence, and it can also happen through a certain persuasion; and indeed, it is rightly achieved through a certain thinning out, and as one might say, through the forgetting and death of the passions. This is indeed the best departure, since the soul draws nothing with it from that which it is being torn away. For as we have found in things manifest to the senses, whatever is plucked out by violence
